status: frozen 2026-11-04 before testing any published merged patch
question: When the paper recorded a merged failure that our own merge of the same two patches does not reproduce, did the code the paper tested lack the agent's changes? We test the paper's published naive-merge patches in our harness.
patch: {model}_naive_merge_k1.patch from the pair's published folder, applied alone to the clean repository and tested against both features with CooperBench's test_solo, once per pair
line_check: an agent's side is present in a merged patch when at least half of the non-blank lines its own patch adds appear among the merged patch's added lines

sets.unreproduced: every pair with an unreproduced merged failure: the re-scoring's 67 features in 51 pairs
sets.pass_one_side: 20 random clean pairs the paper recorded as passing whose published merged patch lacks one agent's side
sets.pass_both_sides: 15 random clean pairs the paper recorded as passing whose published merged patch has both sides
sets.reproduced: 15 random census pairs with a reproduced clean-merge failure (our clean re-merge also fails it) and a non-empty published merged patch

measurements.published: per feature, whether the paper's published merged patch passes in our harness
measurements.same_error: for unreproduced features that fail, whether our output contains the first error line of the paper's output

decision_rule: Primary: among unreproduced features whose published merged patch is not empty, the share that also fails when we test that patch. At least 80%: the code in the paper's merged patch, not our environment or flaky tests, explains why our re-merge passes. The census's robust share (failures our re-merge reproduces) then becomes the main estimate, and we count how many of the paper's clean-merge failures rest on merged patches that lack an agent's side. Below 50%: the published patch fails no more often than our re-merge, so the cause is our environment or flaky tests, and the next step repeats the tests. In between: reported as mixed. Controls: on pass_both_sides the published patch must pass at least 90% of features in our harness, or our harness disagrees with the paper's and the primary result cannot be read. On pass_one_side, the share of features that fail says whether published patches lacking a side are the code the paper tested; if most fail, they are not, and the line check cannot be used to count affected pairs. Secondary: same_error.
results: merge_check_rows.csv and merge_check_summary.json in the output directory
